subject: PDX Clinic — VPC/on-prem residency & air-gap qualification (post-call recap)
messages:

Subject: PDX Clinic — VPC/on-prem residency & air-gap qualification (post-call recap)

Elena, Carlos — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Highlights / pain points you described:
- Regulatory driver: certain clinical AI workflows must remain within PDX-owned datacenter; no persistent egress to public internet allowed for PHI-handling model inference.
- Air-gap preference on high-risk workloads: customer requirement to be able to operate in an isolated environment with offline model sync and manual approval for updates.
- Network constraints: restricted outbound connections, strict egress controls that require explicit firewall rules and a NAT-proxy pattern; vendor appliances must connect only to a narrow set of IPs.
- Key management: HSM/KMS integration required; Redwood-managed keys are not acceptable for the air-gapped environment.
- Procurement: procurement will need a SOC2-type artifact and a short architecture diagram for internal review.

Goals we heard:
1) Validate feasibility for a private deployment (VPC-hosted within PDX tenant or on-prem appliance) that meets the no-egress policy for inference traffic.
2) Produce an initial reference architecture for both a non-air-gapped VPC with strict egress gateway and an air-gapped on-prem option with offline model delivery.
3) Run a technical deep-dive with netops and your security team next week.

Immediate next steps (owners / tentative dates):
- Redwood to share a short constraints doc and suggested architecture options (LAURA) — attached: pdx_requirements_snapshot.pdf, pdx_network_constraints.xlsx — by EOD Thursday 3/30.
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with PDX netops + security, include Solutions Architect (Ben / Tessa) — proposed: 4/2 or 4/3. Laura to send poll.
- PDX to share procurement checklist and point Rajiv Singh from legal for any compliance questions (Elena).

Attachments referenced: pdx_requirements_snapshot.pdf; pdx_network_constraints.xlsx.

Thanks again — we will treat the constraints as blocking for Hosted API and focus the design on private / on-prem patterns.

Best,

Laura — thanks for the recap and for capturing the constraints clearly. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement timeline: we are targeting a decision window by the end of April. Legal will want to see SOC2 + encryption/KMS details before sign-off; Rajiv (copied below) will be the point on legal review but he may request a redline on contract terms.
2) Egress: for the air-gapped workloads we expect zero persistent outbound connections. For the VPC option, any allowed outbound will be through a controlled NAT/proxy appliance we manage; Redwood would need to support an IP allowlist and provide a short list of endpoints for approval.
3) HSM/KMS: our security team will insist on customer controlled keys and an on-prem HSM or cloud-managed HSM that we control; please note that using Redwood-managed keys will be a blocker.

I attached a short internal note that outlines our network guardrails. Also confirm whether your model sync process can be driven by an offline bundle and manual push rather than an automatic check-in.

Carlos and I are available for a technical deep-dive on 4/2 morning Pacific or 4/3 afternoon.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PDX Clinic — VPC/on-prem residency & air-gap qualification (post-call recap)

Elena / Carlos — Ben here (Solutions Engineer). Appreciate the clear constraints. A few technical notes so the deep-dive is focused: 

- Offline model sync: yes — we support producing signed model bundles that can be delivered out-of-band. On the air-gapped path we can provide a validated bundle plus a checksum and a manual ingestion flow; no automatic outbound calls are required.
- Egress pattern options:
  1) VPC pattern: Redwood runtime runs in a customer-controlled VPC; telemetry and control plane calls can be routed to a single egress proxy you manage. We will provide a small set of IPs and TLS endpoints to allow-list.
  2) Air-gapped appliance: on-prem containerized runtime that consumes the signed model bundle. No outbound during inference. Admin update window for pulling bundles via secure thumb drive or a sanctioned outbound jump host.
- KMS/HSM: both options support customer-managed keys. For cloud-HSM we integrate with key wrap and can accept keys provisioned in your cloud tenant. For on-prem HSM we can integrate with PKCS#11-backed keystores; we will need a short integration checklist from your team.

For the upcoming call we suggest the following agenda to keep it actionable:
1) Netops: firewall rules, allowed outbound patterns, IP allowlist process (20 min)
2) Security: KMS/HSM approach and compliance artifacts required (20 min)
3) Ops: model sync / lifecycle for air-gapped workloads and acceptance testing (15 min)
4) Next steps & timelines (5 min)

Would you prefer 4/2 9:00–10:00am PT or 4/3 2:00–3:00pm PT? I can draft a lightweight reference architecture for each option prior to the call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
